short.title: Paw Prints in 4000-Year-Old Anatolian Brick #Shorts
short.hook: Paw prints in 4,000-year-old bricks at Tavşanlı Höyük—Mehmet Nuri Ersoy, Turkey’s Minister of Culture and Tourism, said they were made by a dog.
script: Paw prints in 4,000-year-old bricks at Tavşanlı Höyük—Mehmet Nuri Ersoy, Turkey’s Minister of Culture and Tourism, said they were made by a dog.
The bricks came from a wall that collapsed during a fire in the Bronze Age.
Excavations revealed ceramics, bone, and burnt wood alongside the prints.
Turkey’s culture minister said the prints were made by a dog.
The site dates back to 8,000 years ago, which is older than the Bronze Age.
Fragments of flint tools suggest early human activity in the area.
Could these prints be evidence of early domesticated dogs in Anatolia?
Tap the link below for the full case file.
short.description:
Paw prints in 4,000-year-old bricks at Tavşanlı Höyük, Turkey, have been identified as likely made by a dog. The site, dating back to 8,000 years ago, includes ceramics, bone, and burnt wood. Turkey’s culture minister attributed the prints to a dog, though researchers have not ruled out other interpretations. The findings suggest early domestication of canines in Anatolia. Source: Archaeology Magazine, https://archaeology.org/news/2026/11/02/paw-prints-found-in-bricks-from-anatolian-bronze-age-building/
Full case file: https://youtu.be/MPYdONlD6A4
Images: Mostafameraji / CC0 / Wikimedia Commons; Frank Schulenburg / CC BY-SA 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons; Erkan Fidan (article author; photographe / CC BY 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons
Some visuals are AI illustrations.
